issues.issue: The right to "repay the Policy Debt in whole or in part at any time prior to the death of the Insured and while the policy is in force" is contradicted by the Overloan Protection list, which provides that "[n]o additional loans or loan repayments will be allowed" once that feature is in effect. Both speak to the same in-force policy.

Condition 2 requires that "the Policy Debt is equal to 96% of the Policy Value" — an exact equality that would almost never obtain — where the following paragraph assumes a loan balance "in excess of 96%". The eligibility trigger as written is likely a mis-statement of an "at least" threshold.

Condition 2 (debt exactly equal to 96% of Policy Value) cannot be reconciled with the next paragraph, which contemplates exercise where "the loan balance is in excess of 96% of the Policy Value" and requires repayment of the excess. The two passages state different entry conditions.

This paragraph presupposes exercise while "the loan balance is in excess of 96% of the Policy Value", but the eligibility list immediately above permits exercise only when "the Policy Debt is equal to 96% of the Policy Value". The two cannot both be satisfied.

Reducing the Total Face Amount to 101% of Policy Value sits against Section 1's Minimum Total Face Amount of $100,000 and Section 5's requirement that reductions be subject to that minimum, with no statement of which prevails. It also triggers no pro-rata Surrender Charge although Section 5 requires one on any reduction.

The bar on all further premium payments conflicts with Section 4's undertaking that "in no event ... will we refuse to accept any premium necessary to prevent the policy from terminating". Nothing in either provision says which yields.

The prohibition on loan repayments contradicts the Loan Repayment paragraph of the same section, which allows repayment "at any time prior to the death of the Insured and while the policy is in force", and sits oddly with the requirement that excess loan balance be repaid on exercise. Loan interest meanwhile continues to accrue with no way to pay it.

The paragraph both imposes a one-time Overloan Transaction Charge (3.5% of Policy Value) and says "There is no additional charge for this benefit", and the sentence is cut off before its object. The reader cannot tell what is charged and what is free.

Condition (c) forbids a withdrawal reducing the Basic Face Amount below "the Minimum Face Amount shown in Section 1", but Section 1 contains no term of that name — only a Minimum Total Face Amount and a Minimum Basic Face Amount. The limit the condition imposes is not identified.

"Any benefits provided are not less than that required by law of the state where this policy was delivered" states an unquantified floor without identifying which law or which benefits it measures. Its operative effect on any particular calculation is indeterminate.

The right-of-first-offer condition — "no transfer of ownership shall take effect unless we or one of our affiliated companies first have the right to also offer consideration" — sets no time limit, no procedure and no consequence if the Company does not respond. Whether it merely requires an opportunity to bid or blocks transfer until the Company acts is unclear.

This restriction on transfers, including "a collateral or absolute assignment", is difficult to reconcile with Section 18, which permits you to "assign any interest in this policy without the consent of any person other than an irrevocable Beneficiary". The two sections set different conditions on the same act.

The paragraph is broken mid-sentence, so the condition preceding "your estate will be the Beneficiary" (evidently the absence of a surviving named beneficiary) is missing. As printed the default-beneficiary rule has no stated trigger.

The freedom to assign "without the consent of any person other than an irrevocable Beneficiary" runs against Section 17, which bars any transfer of ownership or collateral or absolute assignment for consideration until the Company has had the right to make a competing offer. The opening words "[e]xcept as otherwise provided in this policy" do not say which prevails.

The adjustment is to the benefit "that would have been purchased at the correct age or sex by the most recent Cost of Insurance charge deducted", a formula that uses one month's charge to reprice the whole face amount and reads as though words are missing. What the corrected benefit is cannot be computed from the sentence.

The operative promise is missing: the text opens "the Issue Date, except for any p ... insurability", so the words stating that the Company will not contest the policy after two years, and the exception, are absent. The core of the incontestability clause cannot be read from the provision.

The recovery is capped at "the higher of a return of any paid premium required by us for the contested face amount or the sum of any Monthly Deductions made under this policy for the contested face amount", but neither figure is defined for a flexible-premium policy where premiums are not allocated to particular face amounts. How to attribute premium or deductions to a "contested face amount" is unstated.

The integration clause is immediately qualified by the statement that later written requests "may become part of the policy", without saying when or how they do so. "May become part" leaves the boundary of the entire contract open.

That open-ended incorporation of later requests is hard to square with the following paragraph of the same section, which requires any change in the provisions of the policy to be in writing signed by an executive officer and countersigned. The section describes two inconsistent routes to amendment.

The reserved "right to correct any clerical errors in this policy, or in our administration of the policy" gives no definition of "clerical error" and no limit on retroactive correction. It could be read to reach substantive figures such as the Schedule's rates and charges.

The opening line is broken ("nniversary-we:will:send-you=-without-charge ach-Policy Year which-ineludes"), so when the statement is due and what it covers cannot be read from the text. The obligation survives only in the enumerated list.

This says the Company "may charge a reasonable fee, not to exceed $50" for an illustrative report requested at any other time, while the next paragraph promises "one report annually without charge". Whether the first annual request is free is not resolved.

The promise of "one report annually without charge" sits against the preceding paragraph, which allows a fee for any illustrative report requested "at any other time". The two fee rules overlap without a priority.

The rider's specification block appears as bare values ("SAME AS POLICY DATE $300.00 75% $250,000 $10,000") with the labels separated from them, so which figure is the Maximum Administrative Charge, the Maximum Proportion Allowable, the Maximum Accelerated Benefit or the Minimum Remaining Face Amount rests on inference. Other rider provisions expressly refer back to these "as specified in this rider".

Defining "We (Our, Us)" as "Phoenix Life Insurance Company, or its subsidiaries" conflicts with Section 3 of the policy, where "the terms 'we', 'us', and 'our' refer only to the Company". The rider states it is otherwise subject to all policy provisions.

The Eligible Amount excludes "any supplemental rider death benefits", a phrase that does not match any defined term in the policy, which speaks of a Supplemental Face Amount and of insurance provided by additional benefit riders. What is carved out of the death benefit is therefore uncertain.

Limitation 3 forbids a Proportion that produces a Requested Benefit "less than the lower of 25% of the policy face amount or $50,000", using a floor expressed through the lower of two figures, while limitation 2 refers to a minimum "as specified in this rider" whose label is detached from its value. The permissible range of election is hard to fix.
